native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: Pottery Form diversity collapsed and Pottery Decoration diversity increased simultaneously in the 18th century BCE (circa 1700 BCE): at the 1700 BCE data point form diversity fell to its sustained global minimum −1.13 (step −1.87 from +0.74) while decoration diversity rose to a sustained +0.97 plateau (step +1.45 from −0.48, later reaching +1.53 by the 11th century BCE); change-point detection flags both breaks entering 1700 BCE and no other century satisfies both onset conditions.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load capital.csv (decimal-comma parsing) and time_series_data.csv; validate the two pottery series are identical on shared centuries (0 mismatches). 2) Primary rules on the decadal series: Form collapse onset = first century at sustained global min (−1.13) with preceding step drop ≥1.5 → 1700 BCE; Decoration increase onset = first century with sustained z ≥ 0.9 (≥3 consecutive centuries) → 1700 BCE; intersection = {1700}. 3) Uniqueness enumeration confirms only BCE 1700. 4) Cross-check with exact penalized-DP (PELT/L2) change-point detection on both series: stable break entering BCE 1700 in both. 5) Sensitivity analysis: stricter decoration thresholds (mean+1SD or global-max anchoring) shift decoration onset to BCE 1000, giving no simultaneous century — flagged. 6) Century naming: BCE-1700 data point → 18th century BCE (1800–1701 BCE), boundary between 19th/18th centuries BCE noted.

sub_hypo.text: Pottery Form diversity collapsed while Pottery Decoration diversity increased simultaneously at the 1700 BCE data point, identified as circa the 18th century BCE. Form diversity dropped by 1.87, from +0.74 to its sustained global minimum of −1.13; decoration diversity rose by 1.45, from −0.48 to a sustained +0.97 plateau, later reaching +1.53 by the 11th century BCE. Only 1700 BCE satisfies both primary onset conditions, and change-point detection identifies breaks entering 1700 BCE in both series. This simultaneity is sensitive to the decoration threshold: stricter definitions shift decoration onset to 1000 BCE and yield no simultaneous century.
sub_hypo.context: Prehistoric archaeological pottery diversity series in capital.csv and time_series_data.csv, identical on shared centuries; simultaneous onset at the 1700 BCE data point, described in the hypothesis as circa the 18th century BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: Unique simultaneous opposing changes at 1700 BCE: form first reaches its sustained global minimum of −1.13 following a drop ≥1.5 (observed −1.87), while decoration first reaches sustained z ≥0.9 for at least three consecutive centuries (observed rise +1.45 to +0.97). Exact penalized-DP (PELT/L2) change-point detection confirms stable breaks entering 1700 BCE in both series. Decoration subsequently reaches +1.53 by the 11th century BCE. Using mean+1SD or global-maximum anchoring instead shifts decoration onset to 1000 BCE, eliminating simultaneous onset.
